one_line: Rashtrakuta emperor Krishna III and Chola crown prince Rajaditya face off at the turning-point battle of Takkolam, c. 948–949 CE.

appearance.age_look: Krishna III appears late 30s, broad-shouldered and battle-hardened; Rajaditya appears late 20s, athletic and agile.
appearance.face: Krishna III has an oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, short boxed beard and calm, assessing eyes with a steady, composed expression; Rajaditya has a slightly longer face, rich brown Tamil complexion, straight nose, neatly groomed moustache, clean-shaven jaw and intense, determined eyes with a focused, heroic expression.
appearance.hair: Krishna III’s straight black hair is pulled back into a low warrior’s bun at the back of his head, partly covered by a simple golden circlet with a small central lotus motif; Rajaditya’s straight black hair is tied in a medium-height topknot at the back-crown, wrapped with a narrow dark-red cloth band and no metal crown.
appearance.costume: Krishna III wears a Deccan-style royal-warrior outfit: a long-sleeved, thigh-length quilted tunic in deep indigo cotton with subtle diamond stitching and a narrow V-neck, over which sits a fitted bronze breastplate shaped in simple horizontal bands; around his waist is a broad maroon-and-gold woven cloth sash, knotted to one side with the ends hanging to mid-thigh, and below he wears off-white cotton dhoti-style trousers wrapped above the ankles, secured with a thin belt, paired with brown leather sandals; his forearms bear plain bronze bracers, and he wears a single long gold earring in each ear, a short gold necklace, and a simple gold armlet on his upper right arm, all modestly sized; Rajaditya wears a Chola-style field outfit: a sleeveless, knee-length cotton tunic in rich dark-red with a subtle vertical stripe texture, belted with a broad mustard-yellow sash that wraps twice around his waist and is tied firmly at the front-left, over a wrapped off-white lower garment (veshti) drawn between the legs and tucked at the back for riding and movement, reaching just below the knees; over his chest he wears a leather-and-bronze lamellar cuirass of overlapping small plates dyed brown, with additional narrow bronze plates strapped over his shoulders; his legs are covered by close-wrapped off-white cloth puttee bindings from knee to ankle, and he wears simple brown leather sandals; his jewellery is restrained: a thin gold neck chain, small gold studs in both ears, and a narrow bronze armlet on his left upper arm.
appearance.signature: Krishna III’s signature weapon is a long Deccan straight sword with a slightly flared tip, iron blade, simple crossguard and a brown leather-wrapped hilt carried sheathed at his left hip, while Rajaditya’s signature weapon is a tall South Indian spear (vel) with an iron leaf-shaped head, a dark wooden shaft and a small fluttering red cloth tied just below the blade.

ref_desc: Krishna III is a medium-brown, broad-shouldered man with a low bun, golden circlet, deep indigo quilted tunic, bronze breastplate, maroon sash and straight sword at his left hip, beside Rajaditya, a rich-brown, athletic man with a topknot, dark-red tunic, leather-and-bronze cuirass, off-white wrapped lower garment and a tall spear with a red cloth tie; both wear restrained gold jewellery in a palette of deep indigo, dark red, off-white, maroon and bronze.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historically grounded South Indian warriors from c. 10th-century Takkolam, shown side by side: Krishna III as a broad-shouldered, medium-brown Deccan emperor with an oval face, neat moustache and short beard, straight black hair pulled into a low bun, wearing a simple golden circlet with a small central lotus, a long-sleeved deep indigo quilted tunic, a fitted bronze breastplate of horizontal bands, a broad maroon-and-gold woven sash knotted at his waist, off-white wrapped dhoti-style trousers, plain bronze forearm bracers, modest gold earrings, necklace and armlet, brown leather sandals, and a long straight sword with a slightly flared tip sheathed at his left hip; beside him Rajaditya as an athletic, rich-brown Tamil prince with an intense expression, straight black hair in a medium-height topknot wrapped with a narrow dark-red cloth band, a sleeveless dark-red knee-length cotton tunic with subtle vertical texture, a broad mustard-yellow sash wrapped twice around his waist, a brown leather-and-bronze lamellar cuirass over his chest with extra narrow plates on his shoulders, an off-white wrapped veshti drawn between the legs for mobility, off-white cloth puttees from knee to ankle, brown leather sandals, restrained gold studs, a thin neck chain and a bronze armlet, gripping a tall South Indian spear with a leaf-shaped iron head, dark wooden shaft and a small red cloth tied below the blade; use a coherent palette of deep indigo, dark red, off-white, maroon and bronze, and present them in neutral, balanced poses showing their face, hair, full costume and weapons clearly from head to toe.
